methods.label: Separate the power terms and the multiples of a
methods.explanation:
Separate the two patterns in the nine terms:
\[
S=(x+x^2+\cdots+x^9)+a(1+2+\cdots+9).
\]
The coefficient sum is
\[
1+2+\cdots+9=\frac{9(1+9)}2=45.
\]
Let \(G=x+x^2+\cdots+x^9\). Multiplying by \(x\) shifts each power up by one, so subtraction cancels the internal powers:
\[
xG-G=x^{10}-x.
\]
Under the assumption \(x\ne1\), division by \(x-1\) is valid and gives
\[
S=\frac{x^{10}-x}{x-1}+45a.
\]
This is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\) when \(x\ne1\).

The omitted case must be handled separately. If \(x=1\), all nine power terms equal \(1\), so \(\boxed{S=9+45a}\). In particular, at \(x=1,a=0\), the sum is \(9\), while choices A and C give \(1\) and \(0\), respectively, and B, D, and E are undefined. Thus no listed expression works for every allowed value as written; choice D needs the additional restriction \(x\ne1\).
